label: History
value: Adrian Treleaven traveled to the ocean at Seven Gulls.
unit: Adrian Treleaven traveled to the ocean at Seven Gulls on his physician's instructions after failing to fully recover from a severe spring bout of typhoid fever, desiring to visit the ancient homestead where his grandparents, the Tremaynes, had lived. Upon his arrival, he joined the Carrows and Lorna Vane in various summer activities across the harbor, rivers, and pastures, during which he worked on a book project. He fell deeply in love with Lorna, but left Seven Gulls at the end of the season after confessing his feelings to Nell Carrow. During his time there, he collaborated with James Garrick on a biography titled The Life-Book of Captain Saul, gathering material directly from Seven Gulls and taking a photograph of Captain Saul for its frontispiece. After the book was accepted for publication, he stayed in Vancouver before writing to request room and board to return to Seven Gulls to court Lorna. They eventually married and had a child, subsequently traveling together to Japan for a year to gather background material for Adrian's new novel.

label: Quotes
value: > Well, they didn’t choose you on account of your appearance, that’s without a doubt. She’s awfully thin and plain, Thirza. Step over this way, child, so I can inspect you. label: Quotes
value: > Come, come, stand up, little one. Naturally, you have my forgiveness. It seems I was likely somewhat overly strict with you, regardless. However, I am simply quite a candid individual. You simply must not pay me any heed, that is all. No one can dispute that your hair is exceedingly red; nevertheless, I used to know a female—we actually attended school together—who possessed hair precisely as red as yours in her youth, yet it deepened into a truly lovely auburn as she matured. It would not amaze me in the slightest if the same thing happened to yours—not in the slightest.

label: Quotes
value: > I must say I am becoming pleased to take a seat. My feet have carried me the whole day, and two hundred pounds is quite a weight for just two feet to haul about. Not being overweight is a major blessing, Thirza. I trust you are grateful for it. Now, Nell, word has reached me that you abandoned your plan to attend college. Hearing that made me genuinely pleased. You currently possess as much learning as is good for a woman’s comfort. Girls attending college alongside men and filling their brains with Latin and Greek and such foolishness is something I do not support.

label: Quotes
value: > Nell has reached eighteen; I had already wed by the time I was that age. We older people, Thirza, tend far too often to believe that kids remain young forever, that is the truth. I trust she will not adopt any foolish romantic ideas while at Wexcombe. I do not endorse those coeducational institutions and never have, that is the truth. I am convinced that those attending such colleges rarely accomplish much beyond flirting.

label: History
value: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby lives at Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley.
unit: Living at Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley, Mrs. Agatha Sowerby spent decades as a central figure in the community, leading church societies and keeping a watchful eye over her neighbors. When Nell Harcourt first arrived at Grey Shutters, Mrs. Agatha criticized her appearance, sparking a fierce outburst from Nell; however, after Nell offered a humble apology, Mrs. Agatha quickly forgave her. Over time, she grew fond of Nell and actively assisted her and the Abernethys, including dressmaking for Nell and managing various church events. When her husband Thomas fell sick and died, Mrs. Agatha nursed him devotedly; facing financial hardship and the sale of her farm, she accepted Thirza Abernethy's invitation to move into Grey Shutters rather than leave Brierley. At Grey Shutters, she remained deeply involved in parish affairs and community gossip while helping raise the children. In her later years, she continued to reside at Grey Shutters, occupying her time by crafting cotton-warp quilts for Nell's future daughters.

label: History
value: Ambrose Kerr grew up as a passionate Grit.
unit: Ambrose Kerr grew up as a passionate Grit in a political family. During a fierce general election fifteen years before meeting Nell, he publicly swore not to shave his face or cut his hair until the Liberals returned to power. He maintained this oath for fifteen years, looking strikingly like an ancient Viking. On New Year's Eve, he joined Captain Saul and others at the lighthouse, entertaining them with stories, singing Scotch ballads in his tenor voice, and dancing elegantly with Lorna Vane. When the Liberals finally won the election, Ambrose forced the barber Gus to give him a haircut and shave before sunrise; his newly clean-shaven appearance shocked his elderly housekeeper so severely that she fainted. Soon after, he married Miss Winifred Tolley. They settled down together in a comfortable greenish-gray house between the Glen and Seven Gulls Point, which Ambrose had landscaped with planted trees, a spruce hedge, and a rose garden. When reports reached his wife concerning the mistreatment of an orphan named Mary by Mrs. Grimble over-harbour, Ambrose traveled across the water to investigate, becoming enraged at the details of the child's abuse.

He maintained this oath for fifteen years, looking strikingly like an ancient Viking. On New Year's Eve, he joined Captain Saul and others at the lighthouse, entertaining them with stories, singing Scotch ballads in his tenor voice, and dancing elegantly with Lorna Vane. When the Liberals finally won the election, Ambrose forced the barber Gus to give him a haircut and shave before sunrise; his newly clean-shaven appearance shocked his elderly housekeeper so severely that she fainted. Soon after, he married Miss Winifred Tolley. They settled down together in a comfortable greenish-gray house between the Glen and Seven Gulls Point, which Ambrose had landscaped with planted trees, a spruce hedge, and a rose garden. When reports reached his wife concerning the mistreatment of an orphan named Mary by Mrs. Grimble over-harbour, Ambrose traveled across the water to investigate, becoming enraged at the details of the child's abuse.

label: History
value: Anthony Tulk is an orphaned nephew of Timothy Cotton.
unit: Anthony Tulk, an orphaned nephew of Timothy Cotton, was taken in by Mrs. Laurence Tulk and enrolled as a student in Nell Harcourt's schoolroom. From the beginning, Anthony displayed enmity toward Nell, glaring at her sullenly and defying her efforts to win his affection. On one occasion, he poured the contents of his slate bottle down Aurelia Clay's neck and left his reprimand with a contemptuous whistle. Despite his disdainful attitude, Nell recognized him as a clever boy, though his noncompliance negatively influenced the rest of the class. During a particularly tense day at school, Anthony swaggered into the cold classroom, made impertinent remarks, and was eventually punished with a pointer until his defiance gave way to tears. However, when news arrived that Nell had resigned, Anthony vented his true distress over her departure by engaging in two deliberate, unprovoked fights with other boys.

label: History
value: Elizabeth married
unit: After her only daughter Elizabeth married and departed for foreign missionary work in India, Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house and suffered terrible loneliness. She agreed to move to Portmaris to keep house for Nell, Honora, and their friends at Tabby's Place, bringing along her gray-and-white cat, the Sarah-cat. Over the course of three winters, she served as a beloved housemother to the girls residing there. She later traveled to India to investigate her daughter's mission field despite her intense fear of serpents.

label: History
value: Barney lived in Brierley.
unit: Barney lived in Brierley as part of the Pullen family, often driving his buggy to local events accompanied by his sister Odette. Harboring a long-standing admiration for Nell Harcourt, he had his sister propose marriage to Nell on his behalf after his father granted him ownership of the upper farm, as he was too bashful to ask her directly. When Nell firmly rejected the proposal, Barney quickly moved on due to his practical sense. He soon turned his attentions to Nettie Scobie, whom his mother favored, and married her shortly after, making their first public appearance as husband and wife at the local church.

label: History
value: Belinda lived at Echo Cottage.
unit: At fourteen years old, Belinda lived at Echo Cottage serving Miss Rosalind Penrose in exchange for room, board, and clothing. Though her true name was Leonora Bowman, Miss Rosalind dubbed her 'Belinda the Fourth' to match her older sisters who had previously served there. She maintained a joyful household with Miss Rosalind, routinely indulging in late-night treats despite wall-mounted newspaper warnings. She formed a warm friendship with Nell Harcourt and Isolde, enthusiastically welcoming them during their visits and helping prepare Echo Cottage for Miss Rosalind's wedding. Following Miss Rosalind's marriage to Mr. Stanhope, Belinda moved with them to Boston, where she suffered from intense homesickness and missed St. Brendan's Island. She later returned to Echo Cottage for summer visits as she grew into a young woman. Eventually, she married Tom, a bricklayer, and returned to attend Nell Harcourt's wedding, where she cheerfully threw rice and old shoes as the newlyweds departed.

She maintained a joyful household with Miss Rosalind, routinely indulging in late-night treats despite wall-mounted newspaper warnings. She formed a warm friendship with Nell Harcourt and Isolde, enthusiastically welcoming them during their visits and helping prepare Echo Cottage for Miss Rosalind's wedding. Following Miss Rosalind's marriage to Mr. Stanhope, Belinda moved with them to Boston, where she suffered from intense homesickness and missed St. Brendan's Island. She later returned to Echo Cottage for summer visits as she grew into a young woman. Eventually, she married Tom, a bricklayer, and returned to attend Nell Harcourt's wedding, where she cheerfully threw rice and old shoes as the newlyweds departed.

label: History
value: Captain Saul grew up in a seafaring family.
unit: Captain Saul grew up in a seafaring family and befriended the local schoolmaster John Tremayne during his youth, developing an early love for poetry and stories. Driven by his nature, he ran off to sea as a young man and spent the next several decades exploring the world as a ship captain. Fifty years before his later years, he suffered the loss of his beloved Margaret, who vanished in a thundersquall. In his travels, he encountered and brought back Laurence Vane from Havana, assuming him to be Rufus Vane. Upon retiring from his life at sea to the lighthouse at Seven Gulls Point, he spent his winters at the Point with his rescued pet cat, the First Mate. He maintained warm friendships with local residents like Elizabeth Russell, Nell Harcourt, Hugh Carrow, and Ambrose Kerr, often entertaining them with fiddle music, tales, and deep conversations by his fireplace. Later in life, he collaborated with Adrian Treleaven to publish his memories in a volume titled The Life-Book of Captain Saul. Before his death at age seventy-six, he willed his global collection of oddities to Little Kit and secured a loving home for the First Mate with Nell.

value: Cedric Stanhope arrived in Brierley
unit: Cedric Stanhope arrived in Brierley from Boston to reside with his grandmother near the shore and attend the school taught by Nell Harcourt. He quickly formed a deep bond with Nell, whom he viewed as a kindred spirit and teacher. As a child, he created imaginary rock companions along the shore and enjoyed books and fairy tales. He brought about the reunion of his father and Rosalind Penrose after telling his father about Miss Rosalind, leading to their eventual marriage. As he matured into his teenage years, he grew rapidly in height, developed a passion for football, and began composing poetry. His poems gained published success, culminating in his initial collection. He attended Nell Harcourt's wedding to Hugh Carrow, driving them to the train station afterward, before making plans to travel abroad for two years of study.

label: History
value: Clementine grew up in a strict Episcopalian household.
unit: Clementine grew up in a strict Episcopalian household in Glen St. Agnes alongside her older sister Harriet. When she was seventeen, her fiancé Martin Crawford drowned in a shipwreck, an event that stripped away her girlhood. Following her mother's death when Clementine turned twenty-five, she swore a solemn oath over a Bible with Harriet never to marry and to live together always. Clementine later began offering music lessons to local children simply because it pleased her, despite her family's comfortable wealth. After Minister John Ashdown developed a deep romantic affection for her and proposed, Clementine realized she loved him in return, but she reluctantly asked for time to think before sending a formal written refusal to uphold her oath. She subsequently spent two months away visiting Portmaris before returning to Glen St. Agnes, where John's young daughter Ida Ashdown later approached her to ask her to marry her father.

label: History
value: Cressy is a wealthy freshman at Wexcombe College.
unit: As a wealthy freshman at Wexcombe College, Cressy quickly befriended Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis, effortlessly bringing them into her expansive social sphere. Highly popular, she was courted by many suitors, particularly Hector and Orlando. She moved into Tabby's Place with Nell, Honora, and Mabel Colby, acquiring domestic skills such as sweeping and dishwashing to adapt to their modest lifestyle. During a summer stay at Prospect Point, she met the Rev. Ezra Hale, with whom she quickly fell in love and sought a proposal. Despite initial opposition from her mother, she successfully stood her ground and gained her family's approval. Cressy excelled academically, earning Honors in Mathematics at graduation. In June following her final year, she married Ezra with Nell serving as her bridesmaid. Later, she wrote to Hugh Carrow to clarify Nell's romantic status, encouraging him to pursue her, and eventually visited Grey Shutters after having children.

unit: Edmund grew up at Hollowmere alongside his siblings, spending much of his time reading, retreat into quiet nature spots, and composing verses. He coined the name "Fern Hollow" for a local dale. He kept his epic poetry writing a secret shared only with his sister Izzy. Following a dare from Grace Ashdown, he rode a stray pig through the settlement and accepted the blame for the incident. When Dan Coyle insulted Edmund's mother and Grace, Edmund challenged Dan to a brawl despite his fear of violence, defeating Dan in the spruce plantation. After suffering from a severe toothache, he determined to travel to Kettlebridge to have the tooth pulled. He also spent time sailing around the harbour with Captain Crawford and Tobias Corcoran.

label: History
value: Flossie attended school in Brierley.
unit: Flossie attended school in Brierley, where she gained a reputation for her skill in walking wooden fences and her skill at knitted lace, for which she won top prize at an exhibition. She frequently challenged and targeted Nell Harcourt, once daring her onto a ridgepole that resulted in Nell injuring her ankle. Flossie was disappointed when she was refused the role of the fairy queen in a school dialogue due to her heavier weight, causing her to become moody during rehearsals. She was also involved in local petty feuds, including a three-month silence with Julia Bell after Flossie made a derogatory comment about her recitation bow. Joining the Regent's class, she struggled with arithmetic but successfully passed the entrance exams with a three-point margin. She went on to attend Regent's Academy, residing at a lodging where she befriended Frank Stockley. At the Academy, she earned a distinction among students for being the most caustic-tongued young woman. Later, when Nell published a prize-winning story in island newspapers, Flossie disdainfully accused her of plagiarizing it from an older publication. She also engaged in eavesdropping on telephone calls made to her household alongside her sister Tibby.

label: History
value: Grace grew up in Juneford
unit: Grace grew up in Juneford as the daughter of Rev. John Ashdown, raising a pet rooster named Adam before her family moved to the manse at Glen St. Agnes. She became sweethearts with Cedric Stanhope, though she felt remorse when he accidentally tumbled into a spring after trying to prove his hair curled naturally. Known around the Glen for her impulsive antics, she frequently tumbled into trouble, such as spilling milk and eggs or confusing the days of the week and shaking rugs in the Methodist cemetery on a Sunday. After learning that parish dissatisfaction might force her father to leave the Glen, Grace single-handedly visited the formidable Lionel Fairlie and convinced him to return to church service. When Dan Coyle insulted her name, Edmund Carrow fought him on her behalf, wearing her blue ribbon on his arm. Following a realization that the children lacked proper guidance, Grace helped found the Good-Conduct Club alongside her siblings and friends to regulate their own behavior. She gave her shoes and cashmere stockings to poor Zilla Clow and publicly confessed her role in stealing Mr. Garrick's field potatoes to defend the innocent Lew Baxters. Later, after organizing a concert with Tobias, she faced grief and anxiety when Ida swooned from fasting and Rupert nearly died of double pneumonia. She eventually befriended Clementine Ainslie, whose bond with Grace helped encourage Rev.

label: History
value: Harriet grew up in an Episcopalian family.
unit: Harriet grew up in an Episcopalian family, suffering the loss of her father at age thirteen and her brother five years later. In her youth, she engaged in a two-year romantic relationship with Lionel Fairlie until a foolish disagreement caused an abrupt breakup. Following her mother's death when her sister Clementine turned twenty-five, Harriet fell into prolonged despondency and weeping; during this period of severe grief, she and Clementine swore a solemn oath over a Bible never to marry. Harriet subsequently lived a retired home life with Clementine in their house on the hill, dominating her sister while providing close intellectual companionship to John Ashdown. When Mr. Ashdown prepared to propose to Clementine, Harriet strictly held her sister to their vow. Later, when Lionel Fairlie began courting her once more after two decades apart, Harriet eventually yielded and agreed to marry him.

label: History
value: Honora attended Regent's Academy.
unit: Honora attended Regent's Academy, where she formed close friendships with Nell Harcourt and Mabel Colby. She gave presentations for the Brierley Village Improvement Society, including one on graveyards. After teaching at Delford and later her home school, she gained her father's permission to attend Wexcombe College, rooming with Nell. Alongside Nell, Mabel, and Cressy Lindsay, she resided at Tabby's Place under the housekeeping care of Aunt Euphemia. Upon graduating with Honors in Classics, she married a handsome foreign missionary and relocated to Japan.

label: History
value: Hugh spent three years in Alberta with his ill father.
unit: Hugh spent three years in Alberta with his ill father before returning to Brierley, where he entered school and quickly became Nell Harcourt's primary academic competitor. Despite early friction caused by his teasing, he developed deep feelings for Nell and retrieved a rose she dropped. When both sought the local teaching position, Hugh generously withdrew his application in favor of Nell's and taught at Pale Sands instead to fund his future college education. He organized and served as president of the Brierley Village Improvement Society and co-wrote newspaper notes under the pen name 'Observer'. At Regent's Academy, he won the class medal, and subsequently attended Wexcombe College alongside Nell, where he led the Freshmen to victory in the Arts Rush, was elected Freshman Class President, served as football captain, and joined the Lambs society. Although Nell initially rejected his declaration of love, Hugh remained a steady friend while working rigorously to achieve High Honors in Classics and win the Cooper Prize. Near the end of his college years, he fell severely ill with typhoid fever; during his recovery, he and Nell realized their mutual love and became betrothed. Following three years of medical studies, Hugh married Nell in the orchard at Grey Shutters. He subsequently relocated with her to Glen St. Agnes to take over the medical practice of his great-uncle, Dr. David Carrow.

label: History
value: Ida moved with her family from Juneford to Glen St.
unit: Ida moved with her family from Juneford to Glen St. Agnes. Having lost her mother at age six, she frequently felt jealous of children with living mothers while cherishing memories of her own. When Mary Stubbs took shelter at the parsonage, Ida showed her great compassion, helped prepare a bed for her in the garret, and learned how to clean plates from her. After Elder Baxter altered the prayer-meeting schedule, Ida and Grace accidentally confused the days of the week, causing them to miss Sunday School and perform household cleaning on Sunday instead. When Mrs. Twiss attempted to adopt Ida under the impression that her father neglected her, Mr. Ashdown refused. During the Good-Conduct Club's self-imposed discipline, Ida fainted from fasting, causing her father intense distress. Following Mary's warnings about stepmothers, Ida worried about her father marrying again; however, after overhearing her father's solitary anguish, she bravely visited Clementine Ainslie to ask her to marry him to make him happy.

label: History
value: Rev. John Ashdown served as the pastor of Glen St. Agnes church.
unit: Rev. John Ashdown served as the pastor of Glen St. Agnes church, living at the aged gray manse in Juneford with his children and Aunt Martha following the sudden death of his beloved wife Cecilia. Often lost in academic reading and theological dilemmas, he frequently neglected his daily routine and pastoral duties, once even confusing burial rites during a wedding ceremony. During a walk through Fern Hollow, he struck up a deep, intimate friendship with Edmund Carrow and later encountered Clementine Ainslie, whose beauty and maternal nature gradually won his heart. After a harsh confrontation with Mrs. Twiss over his neglect as a father, Ashdown wrestled with his shortcomings and sought counsel from Mrs. Carrow. Eventually realizing his love for Clementine, he proposed to her; however, she sent him a formal rejection, leaving him heartbroken and convinced he could never love another woman. Struggling with his duties, he later agonized over having to discipline his son Rupert, unable to bring himself to carry out the punishment.

label: Personality
value: Kit is a solid boy.
unit: Kit is a solid, dependable boy who never breaks a promise and speaks sparingly. He is skeptical by nature, preferring to personally test assertions for scientific truth rather than taking them on trust. Protective of others and highly regarded as the squarest boy in Glen St. Agnes, he can handle troublesome companions like Mary Stubbs easily. Unlike his brother Edmund, he takes pleasure in occasional brawls and mock fights.

label: History
value: Kit Carrow was born at the small house beside the harbour coast.
unit: Kit Carrow was born at the small house beside the harbour coast as the child of the House of Dreams. As an infant, his mother Nell broke a strict pact with Hugh to avoid baby talk upon holding him for the first time, and she persisted in calling him Little Kit—a habit continued by Tabitha that Kit grew to detest by age thirteen. He grew up deeply attached to Fern Hollow, hanging sleigh-bells on the tangled Tree Lovers trees and frequently foraging and fishing there. He gained a reputation at school as a chieftain who engaged in sports and fights, contrasting with his brother Edmund. While visiting Grey Shutters, he became the most cherished child of Aunt Thirza. Later, he showed Mary Stubbs his inherited collection of oddities in the Hollowmere attic and showed great competence in handling her outbursts. As he matured, he began preparing for the entrance examination for Regent's Academy by staying after school and studying in the garret, gradually spending less evening time in Fern Hollow. Prior to leaving for Port Marlow to attend the Academy, he shared a final evening gathering in Fern Hollow with his companions and expressed a deep yearning to become a famous soldier and general.

unit: Kit Carrow was born at the small house beside the harbour coast as the child of the House of Dreams. As an infant, his mother Nell broke a strict pact with Hugh to avoid baby talk upon holding him for the first time, and she persisted in calling him Little Kit—a habit continued by Tabitha that Kit grew to detest by age thirteen. He grew up deeply attached to Fern Hollow, hanging sleigh-bells on the tangled Tree Lovers trees and frequently foraging and fishing there. He gained a reputation at school as a chieftain who engaged in sports and fights, contrasting with his brother Edmund. While visiting Grey Shutters, he became the most cherished child of Aunt Thirza. Later, he showed Mary Stubbs his inherited collection of oddities in the Hollowmere attic and showed great competence in handling her outbursts. As he matured, he began preparing for the entrance examination for Regent's Academy by staying after school and studying in the garret, gradually spending less evening time in Fern Hollow. Prior to leaving for Port Marlow to attend the Academy, he shared a final evening gathering in Fern Hollow with his companions and expressed a deep yearning to become a famous soldier and general.

After Rufus suffered a severe head injury in a brawl and lost his memory and faculties, Lorna spent eleven years caring for him in isolation while supporting herself by leasing her farm and occasionally taking in summer lodgers. Upon becoming neighbors with Nell Harcourt, Lorna initially struggled with envy toward Nell's happiness but soon confessed her feelings, forming a profound friendship. label: History
value: Following her mother's death, Lucy and Robin were taken into Grey Shutters.
unit: Following her mother's death, Lucy and her twin brother Robin were taken into Grey Shutters by Thirza Abernethy to be raised alongside Nell Harcourt. Despite Robin's mischievous antics—such as pushing her into mud pies or pulling her curls—Lucy maintained her quiet, neat, and decorous nature. She adapted easily to Thirza's household, diligently performing chores, learning religious verses submissively, and quietly attending community gatherings like the Aid Society. When her uncle Richard Farrow passed away, leaving a trust fund for the twins, Lucy was delighted to learn that Grey Shutters would be her permanent home. During a severe severe hailstorm that terrified others, Lucy remained remarkably serene and held Nell's hand without panic. Even when she tumbled down the cellar stairs at eight years old, skinning her nose, or when Nell departed, her steady composure remained unshaken. As she grew older, her dependability, helpfulness, and mature caution made her a trusted caretaker around Grey Shutters.

value: > It does—yet I entertain no jealousy. I hold affection for Nell, and Cyril pleases me. label: History
value: Mabel befriended Nell Harcourt while attending Regent's Academy.
unit: While attending Regent's Academy, Mabel befriended Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis, forming part of a circle of contemplative and driven scholars. After finishing her third year at Regent's, she spent years working as a schoolteacher in an isolated country school, instructing students across nine grades. Tired of the heavy demands and misconceptions surrounding rural teaching, she decided to attend Wexcombe College as a Sophomore. Mabel rented Tabby's Place alongside Nell, Honora, and Cressy Lindsay, with her Aunt Euphemia taking over household duties and Mabel managing the household financial records. During her time at college, she actively participated in literary activities, including reading old Story Club manuscripts and writing essays for the Philomathic Society. After completing her studies, she moved to Vancouver, where she took up work as a schoolteacher.

label: History
value: Nell's parents died of fever.
unit: Orphaned in infancy when both her parents died of fever, Nell was taken in by Mrs. Thomas and later lived upriver with Mrs. Rudge, assisting with young children. Following a brief stay in an orphan asylum at Marden, she was brought to Grey Shutters by Obed and Thirza Abernethy, where she found a loving home. Nell attended school at Brierley, engaging in intense academic competition with Hugh Carrow and forming lifelong bonds with Isolde Pembroke and other local youths. She co-founded and served as secretary for the Brierley Village Improvement Society while pursuing her studies at Regent's Academy. Nell went on to attend Wexcombe College, excelling in English and winning a prize for her short story writing. After working as a teacher for three years, she married her former academic rival Hugh Carrow and became a mother.

unit: Orphaned in infancy when both her parents died of fever, Nell was taken in by Mrs. Thomas and later lived upriver with Mrs. Rudge, assisting with young children. Following a brief stay in an orphan asylum at Marden, she was brought to Grey Shutters by Obed and Thirza Abernethy, where she found a loving home. Nell attended school at Brierley, engaging in intense academic competition with Hugh Carrow and forming lifelong bonds with Isolde Pembroke and other local youths. She co-founded and served as secretary for the Brierley Village Improvement Society while pursuing her studies at Regent's Academy. Nell went on to attend Wexcombe College, excelling in English and winning a prize for her short story writing. After working as a teacher for three years, she married her former academic rival Hugh Carrow and became a mother.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy lived on Grey Shutters
unit: Obed Abernethy lived on his farm, Grey Shutters, in Brierley alongside his sister Thirza. Seeking a young boy from an asylum to help on the farm as he aged, Obed went to the Alder River station to collect him, only to discover a young girl, Nell Harcourt, sent by mistake. Unable to break the news to her, Obed brought her back to Grey Shutters and quietly insisted that she be allowed to stay. Over the years, he developed a deep bond of mutual affection with Nell, spoiling her and taking great pride in her academic successes. Prior to Nell's departure for higher studies, Obed passed away at Grey Shutters following his ongoing heart trouble. Years after his passing, Nell continued to remember him as the first person who gave her affection and understanding, faithfully visiting his grave in the Brierley cemetery.

value: Odette was saved by Gorham Pullen

She attended school under Mr. Pidgeon and was active in games and plays with her circle of friends, as well as the local Story Club. Odette attended Regent's Academy alongside several Brierley scholars, excelling in domestic science and earning a Second Class teacher's license. Upon graduating, she accepted a teaching position in Stonebridge, where she became well-regarded and earned a spot on the Inspector's Roll of Honor, though she privately found teaching tedious. As a member of the Brierley Village Improvement Society, she served on committees, including the Delford road fundraising path and visiting Judson Tibbs for moral support. She later gave up her Stonebridge post and traveled West to teach on the western prairies. While living in the West, she met Mr. Inglis, a wealthy man from Winnipeg, and returned to Brierley to marry him in a grand wedding before moving to Winnipeg.

label: History
value: Opal attended Brierley school
unit: Opal attended Brierley school alongside Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Odette Pullen, where she participated in the Story Club and was known for her romantic, sentimental writing style. She went on to attend Regent’s Academy to train as a teacher, where she was considered the most beautiful girl in her year and was frequently escorted home by Hugh Carrow. After graduating, she secured a teaching position at Delford school and spent her weekends gathering with her former classmates. She accumulated numerous suitors, receiving and rejecting proposals from Nelson Atkins and the Tullyvale schoolmaster. Following a bout of congestion during the winter, Opal contracted galloping consumption, forcing her to step away from teaching, though she held onto hopes of instructing at Pale Sands school in the autumn. She spent her final summer receiving visits from friends, reconciling past school feuds, and confiding her fear of dying young and entering an unfamiliar afterlife to Nell. She passed away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter and was buried in Brierley cemetery.

After graduating, she secured a teaching position at Delford school and spent her weekends gathering with her former classmates. She accumulated numerous suitors, receiving and rejecting proposals from Nelson Atkins and the Tullyvale schoolmaster. Following a bout of congestion during the winter, Opal contracted galloping consumption, forcing her to step away from teaching, though she held onto hopes of instructing at Pale Sands school in the autumn. She spent her final summer receiving visits from friends, reconciling past school feuds, and confiding her fear of dying young and entering an unfamiliar afterlife to Nell. She passed away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter and was buried in Brierley cemetery.

label: History
value: Pettifer relocated from New Brunswick.
unit: After relocating from New Brunswick, he acquired a property next to the Abernethy farm in Brierley. He initially maintained an independent bachelor household, hiring John Henry Carter as a helper. He formed a warm friendship with Nell, often exchanging visits with her and listening to her news. Following a deathbed promise made to his sister in Scottsford, he proposed to Emily Scott, who accepted and relocated with him. Though he and Emily experienced domestic friction over housekeeping standards and his parrot Nutmeg, he settled into married life. He offered blunt advice and editorial feedback on Nell's writing efforts and subsequently took on duties delivering local mail.

label: History
value: Ezra studied theology at St. Columbia
unit: Ezra studied theology at St. Columbia after graduating from Wexcombe. During a summer break, he assumed responsibility for the Point Prospect Mission Church while boarding at Cousin Emily's rooming house. There he bonded with Cressida Lindsay through boating, fishing, and evening walks, as well as inspiring her through his powerful preaching. Though initially hesitant to ask for Cressy's hand in marriage due to his lack of wealth, the two became engaged. After overcoming the initial rage of Cressy's mother, Ezra visited Mount Holly where both of her parents grew fond of him. The couple married the following June. By the time of Nell and Hugh's September wedding, Ezra delivered what was praised as a most beautiful wedding prayer, and he and Cressy had welcomed infants into their family.

value: Mary Joe died.
unit: Following the death of his mother, Mary Joe, eight-year-old Robin and his twin sister Lucy were taken from East Welby to live at Grey Shutters by their relative Thirza Abernethy. During the journey, his restless activity severely anxious Thirza, but he quickly warmed up to his guardians, developing a deep affection for Nell Harcourt. At Grey Shutters, he became notorious for constant mischief, such as leaning over the well to find out where the dark goes, plucking tail feathers from Mr. Pettifer's bird, and falling off a pantry table into lemon pies. Nell helped smooth over his religious confusion and persuaded him to keep clean. Upon enrolling in school, he befriended his desk mate Milty Gammon, went fishing with him and the Cottons, and engaged in typical schoolyard games. Though initially harboring a dislike for Cedric Stanhope due to Nell's praise, Robin grew to like him after starting school. Over time, he outgrew his troublemaking ways, grew taller, developed a strong interest in agriculture, and sought permission to manage the Grey Shutters farm in the coming year.

label: History
value: Rosalind grew up in Welby.
unit: Rosalind grew up in Welby and was named by her father after the lavender that kept him awake thinking of her mother. In her youth, she was considered a major beauty and was betrothed to Stephen Stanhope, but after a quarrel twenty-five years prior, the engagement ended and he departed for the United States. Following her mother's death, she remained at Echo Cottage—an ancient stone house—and hired a series of young Bowman girls as helpers, calling each one 'Belinda'. She withdrew from broader social life, leading many to forget her, though she formed a close, warm friendship with Nell Harcourt. Upon Stephen Stanhope's return, the two reconciled, walked together, and were married in an informal ceremony in her honeysuckle arbor. After their wedding, she traveled to the Pacific coast and settled into a new home, later returning to Echo Cottage for summer stays.

Following her mother's death, she remained at Echo Cottage—an ancient stone house—and hired a series of young Bowman girls as helpers, calling each one 'Belinda'. She withdrew from broader social life, leading many to forget her, though she formed a close, warm friendship with Nell Harcourt. Upon Stephen Stanhope's return, the two reconciled, walked together, and were married in an informal ceremony in her honeysuckle arbor. After their wedding, she traveled to the Pacific coast and settled into a new home, later returning to Echo Cottage for summer stays.

label: History
value: Rufus Vane spent his winters working as a clerk.
unit: Rufus Vane spent his winters working as a clerk in his father Abner's store at the Glen and his summers sailing. He pursued Lorna West relentlessly due to her beauty and her initial refusals to speak to him. After her mother nagged her into agreeing, Lorna married him. Following their marriage, they settled on the Ainslie place for the winter. Growing tired of peaceful domestic life, Rufus departed the next spring aboard the vessel Four Sisters with his double cousin, Laurence Vane, bound for Havana. While in Cuba, Rufus contracted yellow fever and died thirteen years prior to the discovery of his fate, while Laurence stayed behind to care for him. For twelve years, the people of Seven Gulls mistaken his surviving cousin Laurence—who had lost his memory in a drunken brawl—for Rufus.

label: History
value: Tabitha Pratt originates from the Glen.
unit: Tabitha Pratt originates from the Glen and belongs to the Baker family. She was hired as a general servant at the residence of Dr. Hugh Carrow and his wife Nell. Though initially suspicious of visitors like Thirza, she quickly developed a fierce and loyal devotion to Nell, whom she affectionately calls "young Mrs. Doctor." At Hollowmere, she became an indispensable member of the household, managing kitchen affairs, baking treats like cherry pies and doughnuts, tending early strawberries, and supervising the children's studies and clothing needs. She stubbornly insists on calling her old acquaintance Winifred Kerr by her former married title "Mrs. Ambrose Kerr" out of deliberate stress. During moments of mystery or fear, such as rumors of graveyard ghosts, Tabitha remains composed, sensible, and unbothered, stepping in to investigate logically.

value: Tessa lived at Hollowmere
unit: Tessa lived at Hollowmere as the youngest of the children there. On one occasion, while carrying a basket of berries picked by Tabitha, she was charged at and chased by Mary Stubbs wielding a giant dried codfish. Later, Tessa was seen studying her primer on the veranda alongside Harcourt while Tabitha knitted.

value: Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters
unit: Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters in Brierley with her brother Obed. Expecting to adopt an orphan boy to assist on the farm, they were mistakenly sent an orphan girl, Nell Harcourt. Although initially planning to return her, Thirza decided to keep and raise Nell, developing a deep, protective affection for her despite maintaining a strict and moralizing discipline. Over the years, Thirza raised Nell into adulthood, supported her education, and eventually coped with the sudden loss of Obed to a heart condition. Following Mary Farrow's death, Thirza also welcomed the orphans Robin and Lucy into her household. Later in life, she suffered from failing vision, though specialists halted the loss of her sight, which eventually improved in her advanced years. She celebrated Nell's marriage to Hugh Carrow, traveled to Seven Gulls to support Nell during the birth of her family, and lived to an advanced age of eighty-five at Grey Shutters, warmly welcoming Nell's visiting children.

unit: Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters in Brierley with her brother Obed. Expecting to adopt an orphan boy to assist on the farm, they were mistakenly sent an orphan girl, Nell Harcourt. Although initially planning to return her, Thirza decided to keep and raise Nell, developing a deep, protective affection for her despite maintaining a strict and moralizing discipline. Over the years, Thirza raised Nell into adulthood, supported her education, and eventually coped with the sudden loss of Obed to a heart condition. Following Mary Farrow's death, Thirza also welcomed the orphans Robin and Lucy into her household. Later in life, she suffered from failing vision, though specialists halted the loss of her sight, which eventually improved in her advanced years. She celebrated Nell's marriage to Hugh Carrow, traveled to Seven Gulls to support Nell during the birth of her family, and lived to an advanced age of eighty-five at Grey Shutters, warmly welcoming Nell's visiting children.

label: History
value: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired by the trustees as the first female teacher in Brierley.
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired by the trustees as the first female teacher in Brierley, a change viewed with skepticism by Mrs. Sowerby and the school trustees. Upon taking up her position, she introduced physical culture routines, biweekly recitation afternoons, and field trips to the forest to examine nature. She also established an after-school study group to offer extra instruction for proficient pupils preparing for Regent's entrance exam. During her time at the school, she addressed student misbehavior tactfully—such as confiscating inappropriate reading material and guiding pupils on moral behavior and clear writing—while successfully maintaining discipline without striking a child. After rumors circulated that she had accepted a job offer at a grade school in her home district, her departure at the end of the term moved her students to tears. She later returned to the area to visit local acquaintances.
